statement: Universities should require every undergraduate, regardless of major, to complete at least one full year of coursework in a discipline far removed from his or her chosen field of study.
City governments should ban private cars from the central districts of large cities and devote the reclaimed street space to pedestrians, cyclists, and public transit.
Governments should allocate the majority of their scientific research funding to projects that promise practical applications within a decade rather than to open-ended basic research.
Public funds that support the arts should be distributed primarily to small, emerging artists and local community programs rather than to large, well-established museums and orchestras.
Schools should prohibit students from using personal smartphones anywhere on campus during the school day, including during lunch and breaks.
Large employers should be required to offer all employees the option of a four-day workweek, provided that total working hours and productivity targets remain the same.
Governments should impose substantial taxes on foods and beverages that contain high levels of added sugar and use the revenue to fund public health programs.
Communities should be required to obtain a fixed percentage of their electricity from renewable sources within ten years, even if doing so raises energy prices for residents in the short term.
News organizations that receive any public funding should be required to clearly label all opinion and commentary pieces and keep them physically and visually separate from factual reporting.
Schools and universities should stop funding competitive sports teams and instead redirect those resources toward fitness and recreation programs open to all students.
